what.title: What an automation is
what.body: A rule that runs on its own: when something happens in your business (a sale is charged, a customer is created), at a time (every day at 9) or when you press Run, it does its steps in order — leave a task, write a note on a card — without anybody in front of it.

first.title: Your first automation, step by step
steps: Pick a card in the gallery and press Use this one: it is created paused.
Look at its steps and change what you want (the amount, the time, the wait).
In Permissions, press Allow everything it needs.
Open Try it to see what it would do with the last thing that really happened.
Turn it on and press Save.

permissions.title: Permissions: why you have to say yes
permissions.body: An automation acts while nobody is watching, so it never borrows your permissions: it can only do what you allowed it, one by one. Until you allow a step, that step is refused when its turn comes and the history says so. If yours has never done anything, look at Permissions first.

worked.title: How to know whether it worked
worked.body: Every time it runs there is a line in its History: when, how it ended and, step by step, what it did. A condition that stopped it is the automation working; a failure says why and what to do. Each run has a reference you can copy for support.

limits.title: What it cannot do yet
items: Starting on its own when something happens in the business: for now an automation on «Something happens» only runs with «Run now»; those on a schedule or a date do start on their own.
Branches: an automation is one column; «Only continue if…» ends it when it does not hold. Two outcomes are two automations.
Counting back from a date of the event («the day before the appointment»): a wait counts from the previous step.
Sending messages, calling another system or asking the assistant or a person: they come in a later version.
The assistant writes drafts: it never turns an automation on nor allows it anything.
